title: Design Weighted LRU Cache
description:
Design a byte-bounded LRU cache `WeightedLRUCache` where each entry consumes a positive integer `weight` toward a total budget `maxWeight`:
- `WeightedLRUCache(int maxWeight)` initializes an empty cache with total weight budget `maxWeight`.
- `int get(int key)` returns the value of `key` if it exists and promotes `key` to the most recently used (MRU) position; otherwise returns `-1`.
- `boolean put(int key, int value, int weight)` stores `(key, value, weight)`:
  - If `weight > maxWeight`, the item can never fit: leave the cache completely unchanged and return `false`.
  - Otherwise, if `key` already exists, remove its old entry first (releasing its old weight). Then, while `currentWeight + weight > maxWeight`, evict the least recently used (LRU) entry. Finally insert `(key, value, weight)` at the MRU position and return `true`.
- `int currentWeight()` returns the sum of weights of all entries currently in the cache.

Aim for `O(1)` amortized time per operation.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to get, put, and currentWeight.
hints: Maintain a standard LRU doubly linked list and hash map `key -> Node(key, val, weight)` plus a running integer `totalWeight`.

On `put`, reject immediately if `weight > maxWeight`; otherwise unlink any existing entry for `key`, evict from the tail while `totalWeight + weight > maxWeight`, and insert the new node at the head. Each entry is inserted once and evicted at most once, giving `O(1)` amortized time.

examples.explanation: Putting (1,10,w=4) and (2,20,w=5) brings weight to 9; putting (3,30,w=7) evicts both 1 and 2 since 5+7>10, leaving weight 7.
Item (2,20,w=11) exceeds maxWeight=10 so put returns false and leaves key 1 intact.
Updating key 1 from weight 6 to weight 2 frees weight first so key 2 is not evicted.
